notes: Covers the core spec: names are appended, every non-public name goes to the internal issuer, a site block's policy is kept, and the names stay listed with auto_https off; but its output still fails the hidden test (likely because it sorts the internal-policy subjects, which also changes existing output, and always emits a policy where the reference emits none), and it silently strips schemes and ports from names.

Closely mirrors the reference: internal names go to the shared internal policy, global options apply via a base policy, site-block policies win, and names are listed even with auto_https off. It silently strips schemes and ports, sorts the internal policy subjects for all cases, misses the hostless-key overlap case, and still fails the hidden test (likely output-order differences); the tests are thorough, including a dummy-site equivalence check.

Parses names strictly with normalization and dedup, and handles site-block precedence and auto_https off, but a list of only internal names gets no explicit internal-issuer policy (it relies on consolidation and runtime defaults), contrary to the spec. It also refactors existing split logic, and it fails the hidden test.

Implements the option with stricter, normalizing name validation, site-block precedence (including hostless-key names), and auto_https-off listing; but because it reuses the split-only-when-mixed logic, an all-internal list (e.g. just `localhost`) gets no explicit internal-issuer policy (the empty policy is consolidated away), unlike the spec and reference, and the hidden test fails.
